After $l\mapsto l/\sqrt\varepsilon$ and the expansion in the external momenta the coefficient of $\varepsilon^0$ of a defect cycle is $\frac1{16\pi^2}\int_0^\infty\Psi(u)\frac{du}u$, with $\Psi$ a polynomial in $f_k(u):=e^{-u^k}$ and $\big(u\tfrac d{du}\big)^jf_k$, $j\ge1$, vanishing at $u=0$, whose coefficients are polynomials in the momenta over $\mathbb Q(i)$ independent of $k$. Since $\big(u\tfrac d{du}\big)^j\big(f_1(u^k)\big)=k^j\big((u\tfrac d{du})^jf_1\big)(u^k)$ and $\frac{du}u=\frac1k\frac{dv}v$ for $v=u^k$, a monomial with $m$ derivatives in total takes the factor $k^{m-1}$; at $k=1$ the monomials with $m=0$ give combinations of logarithms of integers with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(i)$ (Frullani's integral) and those with $m\ge1$ give values in $\mathbb Q(i)$ (Gamma integrals at integers). A coefficient is therefore $\tfrac1k$ times its logarithmic part at $k=1$ plus a polynomial in $k$ over $\mathbb Q(i)$, and $1$ and the logarithms of the primes are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q(i)$ (Lindemann's theorem and unique factorisation).

by: In the untwisted regularised computation of this chapter, at zero finite renormalisation of the operators, the one-loop supersymmetry variation $Q_1$ gives $0$ for the Konishi entry, the structure of [BK] for $\beta\beta$ and $\beta b\to\gamma\gamma$, and unequal colour words with a $\log\tfrac32$ for $b\gamma$ and $\beta b\to\beta\,\partial c$. The twisted one-loop supercharge adds to $Q_1$ the one-loop BRST variation, whose outputs contain the ghost derivative $\partial_{\dot\alpha}c$, in the $\mathcal Q$-class of a multiple of $\bar\lambda_{\dot\alpha}$, and the gaugino-antifield term of the representative of $b$, which is $F_{++}$ plus that term. With them, computed with the gauge-fixing operator of Chapter 3, the Konishi entry is nonzero, every $\log\tfrac32$ cancels, every entry has the colour words of [BK], and the eight pair channels agree with [BK] up to one common constant. A finite mixing of the weight-$3$ operator $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi[\Phi,\Phi])$ with $\operatorname{tr}\bar\lambda\bar\lambda$, a finite renormalisation acting on three letters, moves the Konishi entry, and the Konishi anomaly appears in the class of $\mathcal Q_1$ on the $\mathcal Q$-cohomology.

by: In a scheme in which the translations are the classical ones, $t_P=-\tfrac13$, with the finite gauge-fixing counterterm $\tfrac{27}{16}\int(\partial^mA_m)^2$ units, the particular finite counterterms of the supersymmetry transformations of the block after Theorem \ref{thm:c12-sol}, the cutoff $e^{-\varepsilon p^2}$ and the Feynman gauge of Chapter 3, the one-loop normalisations of $Q$ and $\bar Q$ multiply to $1+(\tfrac{77}{12}+2\log\tfrac32)$ units. A finite field-strength renormalisation of the scalars and the gauge field relative to the gauginos changes this product, and the cutoff $e^{-(\varepsilon p^2)^k}$ replaces $2\log\tfrac32$ by $\tfrac2k\log\tfrac32$ (Corollary \ref{cor:c12-inv}): like the individual normalisations of $Q$, $\bar Q$, $S$, $\bar S$, $K$, these products are conventions of the scheme.
